sentences.text: Learned counsel for the petitioner has contended that petitioner Naresh Vij was not employed with Instrumentation Ltd, Kota at the time of the alleged inspection allegedly conducted by health authorities.

It has further been added that trial court, while trying trial in respect of other co-accused persons, apart from present petitioner, proceedings against whom were stayed by this court, has already discharged them vide order dt. 16.12.2017, as such there could be no offence against the present petitioner as well and has submitted to pass appropriate directions to learned court below, in light of judgment passed in criminal case no.

sentences.text: Learned Public Prosecutor has not controverted factual aspect.

Learned counsel for the petitioner has placed on record copy of judgment passed by learned ACJM No. 7, Kota in Criminal Case No. 14/2012 dt. 16.12.2017 disclosing that out of eleven accused persons, except present petitioner, rest accused persons namely M.K. Dixit, Kalakumari, Rajkumari Upadhayay, Prem Niwas, Santosh Kumar, Anand Kumar, Ramchandra Uddhav, Savarmal have been discharged.

This court has earlier passed an order dt. 18.02.2013 directing court below that criminal proceedings qua the petitioner in the form of criminal case No. 101/2012 (122/1996) State Vs.
Naresh Vij & Ors, shall remain stayed for a period of six months.

Author: G R Moolchandani Bench: G R Moolchandani
HIGH COURT OF JUDICATURE FOR RAJASTHAN  BENCH AT JAIPUR  S.B. Criminal Miscellaneous (Petition) No. 334/2013 Major General Naresh Vij (Retd.) s/o Late Shri Hari Dutt Ji Vij,
aged about 74 years, at present Director, Hinduja Hospital,
Mahim, Mumbai-400016  ----Petitioner  Versus 1. State Of Rajasthan State of Rajasthan through its PP 2. Food Inspector, Office of Chief Medical & Health Officer, Kota.
 ----Respondent For Petitioner(s) : Mr. Arvind Gupta For Respondent(s) : Ms. Meenakshi Pareek, PP.
 HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE G R MOOLCHANDANI  Order 15/03/2018
Criminal proceedings in criminal case No.101/2012 (122/1996) State vs. Naresh Vij and others,
pertaining to offence Section 7/16 of Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, pending before the court of ACJM No.7 Kota, have been assailed.
opennyai_summary.arguments: Learned counsel for the petitioner has contended that petitioner Naresh Vij was not employed with Instrumentation Ltd, Kota at the time of the alleged inspection allegedly conducted by health authorities.
opennyai_summary.decision:
This court has earlier passed an order dt. 18.02.2013 directing court below that criminal proceedings qua the petitioner in the form of criminal case No. 101/2012 (122/1996) State Vs.
Naresh Vij & Ors, shall remain stayed for a period of six months.
Obviously the inspection and offence relates to 21.10.1994, so discrepancy pertaining to case number appears to be redundant.
In view of the above, a direction is given to learned trial court to hear and decide case qua present petitioner Naresh Vij in light of the judgment earlier passed on 16.12.2017 in accordance with law within a period of six months from the date of receipt of copy of this judgment.
Instant petition stand disposed of in aforesaid terms.
